question.problem:
Find the solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -4 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -16 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the matrix on the left-hand side is invertible, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & ={[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9\cdot 8-(-2)\cdot (-2)}[\begin{aligned}8 & 2 \\ 2 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}11 \\ -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{68}[\begin{aligned}68 \\ -68\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
